title: Health: news, or background?
question: Is an injury or a recovery the article's news, or old news retold?
input_note: 6 articles: 4 tune (627, 892, 998, 1020), 2 test (723, 856), no check side. All six split on reports_his_health; 723 and 856 also split on fact and firmness; 856 also on centrality (settled by rule A, not by this boundary).
readings: Main-news reading: health is yes only when the injury or recovery is what the article is about, so health yes goes with fact = health and nothing else.
Any-status reading: health is yes whenever the text says how he is now (recovering, recovered, needed no surgery, out until a date), even in one aside line, whoever says it.
Who-says-it reading: health is yes when someone named in the article (he, his team, the UFC, a named outlet) states his condition or a change in it; the writer's own recap or gloss is background.
signals: Who says the health line: a named source ('MMA Fighting reports', 'Topuria wrote on his website', Dana White) or the writer's own voice ('parece que esta recuperado', 'todo apunta a 2027').
What the line says: a change in his state (no surgery needed, cleared, recovered, out until a date) or just the list of injuries from the fight.
Tense and anchor: tied to the past fight ('suffered in the bout', 'the fight that ended with him fracturing...') or about now ('is recovering', 'did not require surgery').
Recall markers: 'cabe recordar', 'as a reminder', or a relative clause hanging off another subject ('Topuria, que ... se encuentra recuperando'). These flag the writer retelling, not reporting.
Grammar: the health line is its own sentence, or a clause inside a sentence about something else (a callout, a roundup of other fighters, the timing of a return).
Position: headline or lead, or a mid or late paragraph after the real news.
Readiness words only: 'ready to fight', 'back when he feels ready', 'out until 2027'. The guide already says these are a timeline (next fight), not health.

rules.name: A. Main news only
rules.text: reports_his_health is yes only when the injury, procedure or recovery is the article's main news about him, so fact is health. A health line beside other news (a letter, a callout, a readiness announcement) is background: no.

examples.why: The news is his video letter to his son (fact personal_life); the 'no surgery' line is a relayed aside, so no.
The news is White's 'ready to fight' (fact next_fight); 'recovered' is the writer's gloss on it, so no.
The news is Pimblett's callout; the eye-injury recovery is a 'cabe recordar' clause, so no.

rules.name: B. Current state, own sentence
rules.text: reports_his_health is yes when the article states his condition now or a change in it (recovering, recovered, cleared, needed no surgery) in a sentence of its own, whoever says it. It is no when the injury appears only inside a clause recalling the fight it came from, or when the line only says when he will be ready.

examples.why: 'MMA Fighting reports that Topuria ... did not require surgery' is its own sentence and a change in state, so yes.
'Ilia Topuria esta completando las recuperaciones de sus fracturas...' is its own sentence about his state now, so yes.
'que, cabe recordar, se encuentra recuperando' is a recall clause inside the callout sentence, so no.
'parece que el Matador esta recuperado' is its own sentence about his state, so yes, even though it is the writer's inference from 'ready'.

rules.name: C. Someone named says how he is
rules.text: reports_his_health is yes when someone the article names (he himself, his team, the promotion, a named outlet or journalist) states his injury, procedure, condition or a change in it, as a statement of its own. The writer's own recap or inference ('he seems recovered', 'he is finishing recovery', 'cabe recordar'), an injury recalled inside a sentence about the fight it came from, and a line that only says when he will be ready are all no.

examples.why: A named outlet (MMA Fighting) states a change: extensive facial injuries, no surgery needed. Yes, beside the letter.
The only named speaker is White, and he says 'ready to fight', not how Topuria is; 'recuperado' is the writer's inference. No (next fight stays yes).
'Esta completando las recuperaciones de sus fracturas' has no source; it is the writer's reason for a 2027 date. No.
The recovery line is the writer's 'cabe recordar' aside inside Pimblett's callout. No.

flips_note: flips counts input articles (all six) whose majority reader answer changes on any disputed question. 723 and 856 are test side and are counted but never cited.
recommend: C. Someone named says how he is
why: Attribution is visible in the text, so a reader with no backstory can apply it: look for who says the health line. It keeps the guide's existing 'only says when he will be ready' carve-out, which is exactly what splits 998 and 1020, where the one named speaker (White) talks about readiness and the recovery wording is the writer's. It costs two things: an outlet reporting a real recovery update in its own voice with no source named gets no (1020's three-fracture status line is lost as health news, though next_fight still carries the return), and a relayed one-liner from a named outlet gets yes even when it is secondary to the real story (627). Rule B has fewer flips but makes a writer's inference from 'ready' into health news (998), which the guide already rules out.

per_article.627: MMA Fighting (named) reports he needed no surgery, in its own sentence. Health yes. Fact stays personal_life (the letter); 'medically cleared' is readiness, not the deciding line.
per_article.723: He himself writes 'both orbital bones fractured, my septum broken, and my foot broken'. Named source, his own statement. Health yes; fact health, firmness official_or_done. Test side.
per_article.856: The fractures and 'out until 2027' sit in the writer's recall of the Gaethje fight inside a roundup of other fighters; no source, and 2027 is readiness. Health no, fact no_fact, firmness none; centrality only_mentioned by rule A. Test side.
per_article.892: The writer's 'cabe recordar, se encuentra recuperando' clause inside Pimblett's callout. No one named states his condition. Health no.
per_article.998: White says 'listo para pelear', which is readiness (next fight yes). 'Esta recuperado' is the writer's inference. Health no (flips the majority yes).
per_article.1020: White says ready; 'esta completando las recuperaciones' is the writer's unsourced status line used to argue for 2027. Health no (flips the majority yes).
